text:
maya: FYI ran a preflight dry-run for a 60d recompute and the console ETA was way too optimistic (estimated 1.5h, actual ~7.5h).
liam: rough — what's the job payload?
maya: ```{
  "tenant": "beta-corp",
  "job_type": "aggregate_recompute",
  "window_days": 60,
  "parallelism": 12
}```
nana: sounds like classic KV-cache coldstart + cross-region routing. did the estimator include the recent routing policy that avoids GPUs in eu-west when slots < 30%?
liam: looks like it didn't. estimator query still reads `routing_policy_v1`. we rolled `routing_policy_v2` last week which penalizes runs that touch >10% hot keys.
sam: can we surface both "expected" and "pessimistic" runtimes in the preflight? ops gets paged when customers see the invoice mismatch.
jordan: agree on two numbers: expected/pessimistic. also show a short explainer: "pessimistic includes hot-key multiplier and cache warmup".
maya: UX thought: default to collapsed advanced with pessimistic shown under "why estimate may be higher". keep main CTA simple.
liam: immediate fixes: 1) patch estimator to read `routing_policy_v2` feature flags and hot-key multipliers, 2) add conservative 2.5x multiplier for jobs touching tenants with recent hot-key alerts.
nana: +1. also add a tag on job metadata `estimate_mode: optimistic|conservative` so billing can reconcile later.
sam: for product: can we add a checkbox "reserve headroom" that will allocate quota tokens (pre-reserve) so other jobs don't evict this job mid-run? Present it as "reduce preemption risk (may delay start)".
jordan: that interacts with the priority allocator. if reserve_headroom=true we should debit a token bucket against tenant quota and reflect it in the quota UI. product needs to sign off.
maya: pasted a quick log snippet from the failed dry-run: ```ERROR RecomputeRunner shard=3 warmup=0.12s kv_hits=0.01 ps=hot-key-throttle```
liam: that's the hint — almost zero KV hits means cache cold and warmup dominated. estimator should model warmup cost as function of unique_keys_shard.
nana: can we also add a telemetry metric `recompute.preflight_variance` (actual/estimate) and fire low-severity alert >1.4 so we can catch estimator drift before ops gets paged?
sam: +1. also recommend we add a console banner when cluster maintenance windows are scheduled — preflight should factor in maintenance/maintenance-overlap penalty.
ops-bot: maintenance notice: `reprocess-gpu-upgrade` scheduled 2026-04-10T01:00:00Z to 2026-04-10T04:00:00Z; reprocess cluster may throttle.
jordan: nice. add that window into preflight calc as a flag `overlap_with_maintenance=true`.
liam: i'll push the estimator patch to include feature flag lookup and the maintenance overlap check by EOD. @ana can you draft the tooltip copy and the collapsed UX?
ana: on it. mock text: "Pessimistic estimate includes expected cache warmup, network routing fallback, and hot-key throttles." will mock screenshot.
maya: i'll re-run the dry-run after patch and post results. ticket created: 5412345678 (recompute-estimate-delta) linking logs and payloads.
sam: I'll prototype the reserve-headroom checkbox and email preview for opt-in chargeback notice.
jordan: once telemetry is in place we can add a chart on the reprocess dashboard showing estimate drift over time. put `recompute.preflight_variance` and `recompute.estimate_error` on that dashboard.
liam: final ask: include sample preflight API response in docs with fields `{expected_ms, pessimistic_ms, reasons:[...], reserve_token_support:true}` so integrators know what to show.
maya: perfect. thanks all — this should cut down a ton of surprise pages.
